kind: Independent source and regression-test review of actual work-copy changes
pending: Full detailed suite and standard simulation were still running when this source review was written; final run outcomes belong to current-summary.json.

appPersistenceGuards.effect: Only the navigation branch between these boundaries changed; begin/act saving, full expected checks, import/recovery, lock, storage event and delayed-presentation guards retain their complete source.

findings.assessment: Correctly reads enemy.turns, remaining enemy HP and lastRoll.hpDamage/retaliation from committed state. hpDamage is the damage actually deducted from enemy HP, including the original phase boundary handling. Does not substitute projected stats or total raw hit value.
findings.basis: src/engine.js resolveRoll vs src/defeat-review.js and src/views.js

findings.assessment: Only unequipped owned inventory items are counted. Locked items remain wearable under the existing engine equip guard. A saved terminal has 47 weapons, 47 armor and 40 relic alternatives, total 134, and no unused talent points. canInvest delegates to the existing pure canAct/talentPreview logic.
findings.basis: Original retained seed-23757 terminal, existing canAct and six new defeat regressions

findings.assessment: Retry consumes no gold, refills HP using the current build, restores enemy opening state, clears nextLuck, recomputes barrier ward, retains inventory/talents/route progress, and requires an explicit existing retry action. Changing gear while dead keeps HP zero until retry. Paid services remain phase-gated.

Dedicated preparation controls reset only UI rarity/slot/page and focus; they do not call transition or saveGame. Ordinary navigation preserves filters. The existing recovery guard runs before navigation and blocks it while memory is protected.
findings.basis: Complete app diff plus real-module recovery harness tests

findings.assessment: Enemy name, warning, counterplay and phase note are escaped. Missing historical lastRoll and descriptions have fallbacks; unavailable talent nodes do not promise an actionable investment.
findings.basis: defeatReviewView and new view regression cases

findings.assessment: One small release module drives both visible product labels; index/package are aligned at 5.14.0. Save VERSION and keys remain unchanged. The prior visible labels were stale at 5.12.0 while the input package was 5.13.0.
findings.basis: Actual baseline/current views diff and independent rendered release tests

findings.assessment: Combat stops measuring an unused outer panel; reward layout reads the owning panel once and skips prepend only when canvas is already first. The actual positioned-canvas measurement, backing-store budget, materials, particles, frame path and cancellation stay intact.
findings.basis: Full effects.js diff; original geometry variables are overwritten in combat before any use; current/equivalence tests are executed independently.

findings.assessment: All original 63 test modules and both fixtures remain byte-identical. New tests assert observable navigation state, original terminal semantics, release output, rendering command dimensions and lifecycle behavior. They retain losing control outcomes and are not a replacement for native browser reachability or controlled performance samples.
findings.basis: Full file comparison and inspection of all four new test files

reportingLimits: The preparation entry is a usability improvement; the input already allowed legal gear changes through its existing inventory. Do not describe the baseline as having no recovery action.
Single-terminal successful replacement branches are post-hoc examples, not independent random runs or a general survival rate.
Command-equivalence tests use mocked layout and Canvas calls. They establish the exercised arguments and buffers, not actual pixels/FPS or physical GPU behavior.
The local save schema, expected validation and complete unknown JSON field handling were not altered.
Source identities must be checked again after any subsequent edit before treating this review as final.

newConfirmedFindings.description: A valid current-schema saved enemy may carry optional warning/counterplay/phaseNote unknown JSON metadata as containers. The new review UI currently stringifies those into [object Object] or joined array data and lets a truthy warning container hide the valid label.
newConfirmedFindings.recommendation: Read string values only for these optional display fields; use the validated label if warning is not a nonempty string, and omit unsupported counterplay/phaseNote from the view while preserving the complete saved fields unchanged.
